Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a design pattern for LLM applications that augments prompts with retrieved context. The typical architecture includes an ingestion pipeline that chunks documents, generates embeddings, and stores them in a vector database. At query time, a search component retrieves relevant chunks using semantic similarity search combined with keyword search. Retrieved passages are injected into the LLM prompt as context, enabling the model to answer questions grounded in the user's data. RAG improves factual accuracy and reduces hallucination compared to standalone LLM generation.
